gentle.label: Gentle
gentle.hint: Very dark sky and limited noise, suited to bright subjects

medium.label: Balanced
medium.hint: The recommended compromise between faint signal and noise

strong.label: Strong
strong.hint: Brings out the faintest signal, at the cost of a brighter sky background and more visible noise

red.label: R
red.hint: Acts only on red, useful against warm color casts

green.label: G
green.hint: Acts only on green, which light pollution filters often leave in excess

blue.label: B
blue.hint: Acts only on blue, useful for adjusting the look of the sky background

stretch.title: Stretch
stretch.description: In a freshly captured frame the values are proportional to the light collected, so the image looks almost black. Stretching redistributes the levels and reveals the faint signal without blowing out the stars.

auto.title: Compute the black point and midtones suited to this image
auto.label: Auto

blackPoint.label: Black point
blackPoint.hint: Sets the level below which every value becomes black. Raising it darkens the sky background, but you lose the faintest signal.

midtones.label: Midtones
midtones.hint: Classic stretch, with a single slider for mean brightness

ghs.label: Hyperbolic (GHS)
ghs.hint: Generalized hyperbolic stretch. Concentrates contrast where it is needed, for example on the faint arms of a galaxy, without blowing out the core.

midtones.label: Midtones
midtones.hint: Adjusts the mean brightness of the image. Low values strongly brighten the faint parts and bring out nebulae.

whitePoint.label: White point
whitePoint.hint: Sets the level of full white. Lowering it increases contrast, but the brightest stars get blown out.

preserveColor.label: Preserve color
preserveColor.hint: The stretch acts on luminance and keeps the ratio between red, green and blue unchanged, so stars and nebulae keep their color instead of turning white. Abracadabra turns it on automatically. With this option the R, G and B curves have no effect.

strength.label: Strength
strength.hint: Controls how much the faint tones are lifted.

localIntensity.label: Local intensity
localIntensity.hint: High values concentrate contrast around the symmetry point and leave the rest of the image almost unchanged.

symmetryPoint.label: Symmetry point
symmetryPoint.hint: Brightness level where contrast increases the most, usually just above the sky background.

shadowProtection.label: Shadow protection
shadowProtection.hint: Below this level the curve continues as a straight line, so the darkest tones, sky background included, are not crushed toward black.

highlightProtection.label: Highlight protection
highlightProtection.hint: Above this level the curve continues as a straight line, so galaxy cores and bright stars keep their contrast instead of merging into white.

curves.title: Curves
curves.description: Drag the line to change the tonal response. Click to add a point, right-click to remove it.
curves.preserveColorNote: With “Preserve color” turned on in the Stretch card, only the light curve has an effect.

gamma.label: Gamma
gamma.hint: Adjusts the overall response curve. Below 1 it darkens the midtones, above 1 it brightens them.

color.title: Color
color.description: The three Gain sliders correct the color cast. Light pollution filters often leave a greenish or reddish background, which you can compensate for here.

saturation.label: Saturation
saturation.hint: At -1 the image becomes black and white. Moderate values enhance the color of nebulae without washing out the stars.

vibrance.label: Vibrance
vibrance.hint: Boosts mainly the dull colors and leaves the already vivid ones almost untouched, so nebulae gain color without colored stars becoming muddy. If you chose a photo filter, this value adds to the filter’s vibrance.

resetView.title: Undo the adjustments and restore the image as it was when opened
resetView.label: Restore as opened
